title: Design: A replicated configuration store built on Raft

defects.quote: Raft was published in 2014 by Leslie Lamport
defects.correction: Raft was published in 2014 by Diego Ongaro and John Ousterhout ('In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm'); Leslie Lamport is the author of Paxos.
defects.note: [multi-part] [secondary-source] The year is right; only the author is wrong. Top results are likely explainers and blog posts; the primary source is the paper itself (USENIX ATC 2014).

defects.correction: ZooKeeper uses its own atomic broadcast protocol, Zab, not Raft.
defects.note: [secondary-source] The primary source is the Apache ZooKeeper documentation and the Zab paper.

defects.quote: A five-node cluster tolerates three failed nodes
defects.correction: A five-node Raft cluster needs a majority of three, so it tolerates two failed nodes.

defects.quote: A five-node cluster will handle 50,000 writes per second on our hardware.
etcd uses Raft and etcd is reliable, so our own Raft implementation will be reliable too.
defects.known_rebuttal: A correct algorithm does not make a new implementation correct. etcd's reliability comes from years of production use, fault-injection testing and many fixed bugs, not from Raft itself. The hard parts of a consensus system lie outside the simple path of election and replication: membership changes, log compaction and snapshots, disk failures and client retries, and that is where home-grown implementations lose data. Six weeks for two engineers is not credible for that scope; embedding etcd or a proven Raft library gives the same design with far less risk.

defects.correction: it will keep using the database

defects.quote: The procedure for adding and removing nodes have not been designed yet.
defects.note: Copy editor (grammar) and structure reviewer (membership change is one of the hardest parts of a consensus system and the section is empty) both flag this sentence; they should be merged into one finding.

defects.quote: etcd uses Raft and etcd is reliable, so our own Raft implementation will be reliable too.
defects.note: Any rebuttal of this claim that cites no retrieved source must be downgraded to consider.

defects.quote: an entry is committed once a majority of nodes have stored it
defects.note: True description of Raft; a rebuttal disputing the fact itself must be discarded.

defects.quote: A five-node cluster tolerates three failed nodes, so we can loose an entire availability zone and one more node besides.
defects.note: 'loose' should be 'lose', but the sentence carries a wrong fact, so the fact finding wins.
